threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: When you still think a small bottle of water costs £1 and not £2.50 from the corner shop, everyone notices.
Caught a bloke in a floral shirt arguing with a lamppost outside the Ritzy. Said it owed him 'rent' for all those years of shiny light. Classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a kid on a bike trying to outrun a tram, then high-fived the driver as he stopped for a red light. That’s Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever notice how people casually post protest signs in the U-Bahn? It’s like public transport doubles as the city’s bulletin board.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local if they can spot the difference between a Pothole and a Street Art installation—subtlety matters in this city.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 21st bus today, driver stopped to let a pigeon cross. Only in San Francisco, right? A little kindness goes a long way on these streets.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists flock to Park Güell but miss the little plaça with live jazz near Verdi. That’s where the real vibe is.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by their hesitation at ordering 'pan con tomate'—they still ask for it toasted and without the tomato.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the bus will come on time—locals know to check the timetable and plan for it to be late, every time.
Caught a guy trying to barter a half-eaten kebab for bus fare on the 3 last night. Driver just shook his head and laughed. Brixton at its finest.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a kid trading Pokémon cards for kebab slices at the playground. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you find a party in an old train station, right next to a real train repair shop. It's like nightlife meets history!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by the way they instinctively know to step off the bus before the delay hits; waiting for BART is for tourists.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus today with two dogs in designer backpacks. Only in SF can you find pup fashionistas commuting in style alongside regular commuters.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just about Gaudí. They miss the tiny, family-run bars where the real stories and local flavors simmer.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the oversized map in their hands, especially when they stop dead in the middle of a busy carrer to check it.
